name: steady: three ticks a minute apart
why: First sight of a run bills awake time from Ready (20 s earlier) and no disk; each later tick bills the 60 s gap for both. 60 s awake is 3333 micro-dollars with 1200 carried.

name: an hour awake costs exactly 20 cents plus the disk
why: 60 ticks of 60 s: the carry makes the sum exact (200000 awake, 1920 disk for 5 GB).

name: tail: the time after the last awake sight is free, the disk goes on
why: Awake at 10:01, asleep at 10:02: no awake charge for that minute, the disk is charged throughout.

name: asleep for two hours: only the disk is charged
why: 120 ticks asleep: 5 GB x 2 h x 384 = 3840 micro-dollars. A month asleep is 5 x 730 x 384 = 1401600, about $1.40.

name: starting is not awake
why: Not Ready (waiting for a node, restoring): disk only, then awake from Ready.

name: meter away for ten minutes: the gap is free, disk included
why: A gap over 150 s bills nothing, and Ready was long ago.

name: late tick within the gap limit is billed in full
why: A tick 140 s after the last bills 140 s.

name: clock steps backwards: nothing is billed
readySince in the future is ignored
why: The Sandbox controller's clock is ahead of the meter's.

name: two sessions awake at once burn twice as fast
why: Awake time and disk are per session, summed over the account.

name: deleted session: dropped, its last minute free
why: A session that no longer exists is not in the observation.

name: order: the credit that expires first is used first
why: Plan credit (ends 5 Nov), then the sign-up credit (30 Dec), then the pack (next year). 3 micro-dollars of plan credit are left; the tick costs 3365.

name: low, then exhausted; overdraft is not owed
why: 5000 micro-dollars left; each tick costs about 3365.

name: zero balance, asleep: disk charges become overdraft and the clock of exhaustedAt keeps its start
why: Nothing is owed for the disk at zero; exhaustedAt stays where it was, which is what the deletion rule counts from.

name: a purchase clears exhausted
why: A Grant that appears between two ticks counts at the next.

name: unused plan credit does not roll over, purchased credit does
why: After the period ends the plan grant no longer counts.

name: a revoked grant (refund) stops counting
why: What was used of it is not clawed back.

name: upgrade: the new plan grant supersedes the old one
why: Starter's grant is revoked when Pro's for the new period is made.
